append.text: **Ps 8:2a = 8:10 *Dómine, Dóminus noster* → *Senhor, nosso Senhor*:** one word twice, as the Latin and the Greek have it against the Hebrew's two names (MS1932 *nosso Dominador soberano* and DM1962 *nosso Deus* both avoid it). Possessive first, so that the second member is heard as the title *nosso Senhor* in apposition — Portuguese has no case to do what *Dómine / Dóminus* does; *Senhor, Senhor nosso* (the Latin's order) is the option, refused because *Senhor, Senhor* back to back is a doubled cry. The stylist's best line; the Latinist passed it twice; the blind reader did not stop at it.
Ps 8:2a = 8:10 *como é admirável o vosso nome em toda a terra!* — *como* holds; eighteen syllables for the Latin's eighteen.
Ps 8:6 *de glória e de honra o coroastes* (MS1932 word for word) — applied, as this row foresaw.
Ps 8:6 *e o estabelecestes sobre as obras das vossas mãos* (= Heb 2:7) — holds with *super*; no reader remarked.
Ps 8:9 *as veredas do mar*: the blind reader again listed *veredas* as unknown; kept (D15).

terms: | admirábilis | admirável | open | Ps 8:2a = 8:10; 41:5 *tabernáculi admirábilis*; the cognate, a step apart from *mirábilis* → maravilhoso (DRB, MS1932). The Greek has θαυμαστός for both, so a merge into *maravilhoso* is defensible on D15's test and is the option in Ps 8 (*admirável* has cooled to "commendable" in everyday speech); no reader objected |
| univérsus | todo (*em toda a terra*; *todas as ovelhas e os bois*) | working | Ps 8:2a, 8:8, 8:10; one word with *omnis* (ἐν πάσῃ τῇ γῇ); 95:9, 104:7 *in univérsa terra* |

| magnificéntia | magnificência | open | Ps 8:2b *Porque se elevou a vossa magnificência sobre os céus*; μεγαλοπρέπεια; 8 verses (grep: 8:2b, 28:4, 67:34b, 70:21, 95:6, 110:3, 144:5, 144:12 *glóriam magnificéntiæ regni tui*). *Majestade* (MS1932) is *majéstas*'s (71:19), *grandeza* *magnitúdo*'s. **The blind reader listed it as a word churchgoers may not know** (and still paraphrased the verse rightly) |

| eleváre (passive, *eleváta est*) | elevar-se (*se elevou*) | open | Ps 8:2b (MS1932); the *se* form for a Latin passive with middle sense (ἐπήρθη), as Ps 7:7a *exaltáre* → exaltai-vos; the Latinist passed it twice; option *foi elevada* |
| super (place) | sobre | working | Ps 8:2b *sobre os céus*, 8:6 *sobre as obras das vossas mãos*; the row *super (comparison)* → mais que stands. 56:6 *Exaltáre super cælos* will want the same |

| infántes et lacténtes | as crianças e os que mamam | open | Ps 8:3, only here (= Mt 21:16, Vulgate fetched to `consult/bolls-VULG-40-21.json`); *infantes* are princes in Portuguese and *lactentes* is clinical; *pequeninos* (DM1962) is left for *párvuli* (18:8, 114:6, 118:130). Cost: *crianças* does not say the speechlessness of *in-fans* |

| perfícere | aperfeiçoar (*aperfeiçoastes o louvor*) | open | Ps 8:3 — the Latin's reading, not the Hebrew's "founded strength". From the stylist, against draft 1 *fizestes perfeito o louvor* (built like *mirificáre* → fazer maravilhoso; "soa traduzida"); DRB *perfected*; the Latinist passed both. Tried on 10:4 *quæ perfecísti, destruxérunt*, 17:34 *perfécit pedes meos*, 39:7 *aures autem perfecísti mihi*, 67:10, and the imperative 79:16 *Et pérfice eam* (*aperfeiçoai-a* is safe; past *aperfeiçoei*) — it fails none. Cost: in everyday speech *aperfeiçoar* is to improve what was wanting |

| destrúere | destruir — **never at the *vós* imperative** (*destruí* = "I destroyed") | working | Ps 8:3 *para destruirdes o inimigo e o vingador*; 9 verses, none of them an imperative (grep: 8:3, 9:7a, 10:4, 27:5, 51:7, 59:3, 79:13, 88:41, 88:45) |
| ultor | vingador | working | Ps 8:3; family of *ulcísci* → vingar-se; MS1932 *vingativo* is a trait of character |
| vidére | ver | working | Ps 8:4 *Porque verei os vossos céus* — the Latin's *Quóniam* + future (ὅτι ὄψομαι), not the Hebrew's "When I see" (MS1932, DM1962 *Quando contemplo*) |
| fundáre | fundar | working | Ps 8:4 *a lua e as estrelas, que vós fundastes*; 11 verses (*fundásti terram* 101:26, 103:5, 118:90 — Ps 118:90 already has *fundastes a terra*) |

| visitáre | visitar | working | Ps 8:5; 7 verses (16:3, 58:6, 64:10, 79:15 *vísita víneam istam*, 88:33, 105:4); *visitai* is safe; the blind reader heard "God makes himself present in his life" first |

| fílius hóminis | o filho do homem (lowercase) | open | Ps 8:5 (= Heb 2:6); the singular also 79:16, 79:18 *super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi*, 143:3 (grep); the plural *fílii hóminum* (23 verses) → *filhos dos homens*. **The blind reader heard Jesus first**, and 8:6 then as said of him — the reading of Hebrews 2, which the Latin's phrase invites too; kept open between man and Christ |

| minúere … paulo minus ab | fazer um pouco menor que (*Vós o fizestes um pouco menor que os anjos*) | open | Ps 8:6 (= Heb 2:7), only here; the Latin says "less" twice (the Greek does not) — read as the idiom *paulo minus*, not a figure; degree, not time (Heb 2:9 *módico* can be read of time). *paulo minus* alone is "almost" (93:17, 118:87 *Por pouco não*). MS1932 *pouco inferior aos anjos* |
| ángelus | anjo (lowercase) | working | Ps 8:6 — the Latin's reading, not the Hebrew's *elohim*; Ps 90:11 |
| honor | honra | working | Ps 8:6 *de glória e de honra*; 28:2, 95:7 *glóriam et honórem* |

| subjícere | sujeitar (*Tudo sujeitastes debaixo dos seus pés*) | open | Ps 8:8 (= Heb 2:8; MS1932); 46:4 *Subjécit pópulos nobis: et gentes sub pédibus nostris*, 61:2, 61:6 *Deo subjécta esto, ánima mea* → *sujeita a Deus*; *sub pédibus* → *debaixo dos pés* (the living preposition; *sob* keeps the Latin's echo sub … sub and is the option) |

| oves / boves / pécora (campi) | ovelhas / bois / animais (do campo) | open | Ps 8:8; *pécora* also 148:10 (beside *béstiæ*), 134:7b *pecus*; *feras* is kept for *béstiæ* / *feræ*, *gado* is the narrower option |
| ínsuper et | e ainda | open | Ps 8:8 *e ainda os animais do campo*; 15:7, 15:9 *ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe* → *e ainda a minha carne repousará na esperança* |
| vólucres / pisces | aves / peixes | working | Ps 8:9; 103:12 *vólucres cæli* |

| perambuláre | percorrer (+ direct object) · andar (in / per) | open | Ps 8:9 *que percorrem as veredas do mar* (L&S "to go through, traverse"; MS1932, DM1962); Ps 90:6 has *que anda pelas trevas*; 67:22, 100:2 are L&S's Church sense "to walk, conduct oneself" → andar. Two renderings for two senses |
formulas: | *Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!* (8:2a = 8:10) | *Senhor, nosso Senhor, * como é admirável o vosso nome em toda a terra!* | open — Ps 8; both verses are built from the same two slots (decisions `domine`, `quam`), so they cannot drift; the stylist's best line |

| *Quid est homo quod memor es ejus? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?* (8:5 = Heb 2:6; 143:3 is the near twin: *quid est homo, quia innotuísti ei? aut fílius hóminis, quia réputas eum?*) | *Que é o homem, para que vos lembreis dele? * ou o filho do homem, para que o visiteis?* | open — Ps 8; **stands against the Latinist (major, twice)**, who wants the Latin's indicatives (*pois vos lembrais dele*; then *que vos lembrais dele … pois o visitais*): held because *que é X, para que …?* is Portuguese's idiom for the question and presupposes the fact, mood is grammar (D2, D24), and MS1932 has the same build. **Ps 143:3 copies the frame** (*Que é o homem, para que … ? ou o filho do homem, para que … ?*) |
| *Ómnia subjecísti sub pédibus ejus* (8:8a = Heb 2:8) | *Tudo sujeitastes debaixo dos seus pés* | open (hangs on *subjícere*) — Ps 8 |
| *Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem* (8:3a = Mt 21:16) | *Da boca das crianças e dos que mamam aperfeiçoastes o louvor* | open (hangs on *perfícere*) — Ps 8 |
